## 1.Study population characteristics

Before modelling the association between greenspace and asthma, we first describe the participating populations.

#### What does the distribution of variables look like?
--> Heatmap
We can first examine lsoa level summary statistics :
1. mean
2. Std deviation
3. SEM
4. Quantile

Stats can be split/combined across study option to return plot/table
```{r, eval=FALSE}
names_region <- list(c("Liverpool", "Sefton"), c("Liverpool"))

ds.summarystat(x = "D$has_asthma", y = "D$lsoa11cd", 
               type='combine', do.checks=FALSE, 
               draw.plot = TRUE, names_region = names_region, 
               metric = "Mean", datasources=conns)
ds.summarystat(x = "D$has_asthma", y = "D$lsoa11cd", 
               type='combine', do.checks=FALSE, 
               draw.plot = TRUE, names_region = names_region, 
               metric = "SD", datasources=conns)
ds.summarystat(x = "D$distance_local_greenspace", y = "D$lsoa11cd", 
               type='combine', do.checks=FALSE, 
               draw.plot = TRUE, names_region = names_region, 
               metric = "5th_Quantile", datasources=conns)

```
---> Histogram : may not be useful for lsoa level analysis

#### Is greenspace distance approximately normally distributed?
This is to be  developed

```{r, eval=FALSE}
ds.qqnorm()
```

#### Does asthma prevalence differ by sex/age/ethnicity/IMD?
For two numeric variables, we can do grouped pearson correlation.

```{r, eval=FALSE}

ds.groupcor(x = "D$has_asthma", y = "D$distance_local_greenspace", 
            index = "D$lsoa11cd", datasources = conns, type = "combine", 
            names_region = list("Liverpool"))


```

For two categorical variables, we can use a chi-squared test.

```{r, eval=FALSE}

ds.chisqr(rvar="D$sex", cvar="D$has_asthma", stvar="D$lsoa11cd", 
          exclude=NULL,	useNA ="no", suppress.chisq.warnings=FALSE,
          datasources=conns, names_region = c("Liverpool",  "Sefton"),
          force.nfilter=NULL, split = FALSE, draw.plot = TRUE)

ds.chisqr(rvar="D$sex", cvar="D$has_asthma", stvar="D$lsoa11cd", 
          exclude=NULL,	useNA ="no", suppress.chisq.warnings=FALSE,
          datasources=conns, names_region = "Liverpool",
          force.nfilter=NULL, split = TRUE, draw.plot = TRUE)


ds.chisqr(rvar="D$sex", cvar="D$has_asthma", stvar="D$lsoa11cd",
          exclude=NULL,	useNA ="no", suppress.chisq.warnings=FALSE,
          datasources=conns, names_region = NULL,
          force.nfilter=NULL, split = TRUE, draw.plot = FALSE)

ds.chisqr(rvar="D$sex", cvar="D$has_asthma", stvar="D$lsoa11cd",
          exclude=NULL,	useNA ="no", suppress.chisq.warnings=FALSE,
          datasources=conns, names_region = NULL,
          force.nfilter=NULL, split = TRUE, draw.plot = TRUE)

ds.chisqr(rvar="D$sex", cvar="D$has_asthma", stvar="D$lsoa11cd",
          exclude=NULL,	useNA ="no", suppress.chisq.warnings=FALSE,
          datasources=conns, names_region = "Liverpool",
          force.nfilter=NULL, split = TRUE, draw.plot = FALSE)

```


## 2. Effect of distance to greenspace

#### Is greenspace distance associated with asthma?

This is a function from dsbase.

```{r, eval=FALSE}

ds.glm(formula = "has_asthma ~ distance_local_greenspace", data = "D", 
       family="binomial", datasources=conns)

```


#### Does the association remain after accounting for individual characteristics?
This is a function from dsbase.
```{r, eval=FALSE}
ds.glm(formula=paste("has_asthma ~ distance_local_greenspace + sex"), 
        data = "D", family="binomial",datasources=conns)
```


### 3. Accounting for geographical clustering

#### Question 3.1 — Is greenspace associated with asthma after accounting for LSOA clustering?
Is distance to local greenspace associated with the probability of having asthma, while allowing baseline asthma risk to differ between LSOAs?
This is a function from dsbase which is based on glmer: a function from package lme4.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
ds.glmerSLMA(formula="has_asthma ~ distance_local_greenspace + (1 | lsoa11cd)",
             family="binomial",
             dataName = "D",
             datasources=conns[1]
             )
```
